title: TUR boot trial record
description: /var/lib/tur/boot-health/trial.json: information about the trial of a new deployment that is in progress (boot-health-and-rollback.md, section 5.2). GRUB's environment block, not this file, is the authority for whether a trial is in progress. The file is written by one OS version and read by another, so a reader must ignore members it does not know. null means the value is not known.

deployment.description: A deployment as bootc status describes it.

transport.description: Transport of the reference, for example registry or oci.

build_id.description: TUR build ID read from the deployment.

attempt.description: One start of the new deployment that reached tur-boot-health classify.

boot_id.description: Boot ID as the journal writes it: 32 hexadecimal digits.

failed_check.description: The first required check that failed, for example R5 or X:name.

event_id.description: Identifies the trial in the history, the notice and the evidence directory.

phase.description: trial from arming; reverting once the previous deployment has begun to make a fallback permanent (section 5.9).

armed_boot_id.description: The boot that armed the trial. Empty if the record was made after the fact.

armed_at.description: Seconds since the epoch when the trial was armed. For people; no decision depends on it.

trial_args.description: Kernel arguments added to every trial boot.

grub_cannot_save.description: GRUB announced a number of tries left that the environment block does not hold: attempts are counted in this record instead (section 5.6).

reason.description: Why the fallback began, once it has.
